parts.title: The Echo
parts.as_of_basis: The vote was cast on Tuesday 4 November 1952; the horizon is noon in Washington the next day. The result is known inside it from Stevenson's concession as the New York Times printed it that morning (src-stevenson-19521105), so the Echo may say who won the presidency and nothing more. Official counts (the electors' votes of December 1952, the Clerk's 1953 statistics) are later records and are never shown as known at the horizon. Truman's own statement of 5 November is not used: its hour is not shown.
parts.picked_after_week_known: This Echo was picked on 2026-11-12, after week 33's lead was known, because the pre-registered echo bank (24 echoes tagged by mechanism before any week's news, bible section k) has not yet been built.

device.reason: The past has no outlet measurement (grey bars only, bible c); balance is carried by period perspectives from both parties in their own words (Truman, Stevenson for the governing party; Eisenhower for the opposition) and three period documents (E1).

fit_gap: Truman gave no reason tied to Korea when he withdrew; his 29 March words are used only for the withdrawal.
The New Hampshire vote is a preference poll inside one party in one state, not a national election.
Congress is not in the mechanism sentence: the 1952 House and Senate majorities were not read from a primary source in this session, and they were settled in the days after the vote.
No leader of the governing party names the war as the reason for the loss inside the horizon (the week's lead has one); none is held.
outside_horizon: the electors' votes of 15 December 1952 and the Clerk's printed counts

no_bridge.ruling: Founder's ruling (chat 2026-11-12, asked directly): the 1952 party names 'Democratic' and 'Republican' are allowed in the Echo as institutions; no person or event from this week's news may appear. 'GOP' and this week's persons and places stay flagged.
no_bridge.also: no 'like today', 'just as', or any sentence pointing at the week, in either direction (bible e)
